text.p: Italian debt futures powered to news highs on Monday, spurred by the weekend passage through the lower house of parliament of the 1997 budget, with no clear sign the market has peaked.

But with investors pinning hopes on a discount rate cut as early as next weekend on the back of what are widely expected to be good preliminary November CPI figures, there is scope for disappointment.
"Inflation figures are out on Friday and we are assuming a rate cut any time after that. If not, the market will be disappointed," said Andrew Carless, a futures trader at Fimat Futures in London.
"It will be interesting to see what happens when we get the lira back in the ERM and a rate cut is out of the way," said another London futures trader.

"We are already hearing a few clients saying the high yielding markets have got ahead of themselves," the trader added. Consensus forecasts are for preliminary CPI to fall to 2.5-2.6 percent in November from 3.0 percent in October.
Chart analysts see a line of support at 127.20 with resistence at 127.90 and a further line of resistence at 128.34.
"There is a problem of a lack of follow-through," said another trader. "There is nothing much that can happen to make the market go much higher with all the goods news priced in."
